title: Cells in development minimize surprise and variational free energy like nervous systems

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cells in development minimize surprise and variational free energy like nervous systems

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Living systems minimize surprise and optimize variational free energy by tuning internal states to best predict future stimuli, and this holds for individual cells during metazoan development as much as for nervous systems.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Systems minimize surprise and optimize variational free energy by tuning their internal states in a way that optimally predicts future stimuli (Friston and Ao, 2012; Friston, 2013; Badcock et al., 2019). This is as true for nervous systems as it is for individual cells during metazoan development (Friston et al., 2015; Ramstead et al., 2019).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity”. Scope: Nervous systems and individual cells in metazoan development

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public time series permit tests of specified predictive models in selected developmental systems. The sweeping law and its contrast with ordinary dynamical models are weakly discriminating unless model classes and priors are tightly prespecified.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit explicit active-inference models and matched non-predictive control models to public time-series of cellular responses during development, then compare out-of-sample prediction of state updates and estimated variational free energy.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cellular surprise is model-dependent rather than directly observed.

Free-energy formulations can be flexible enough to fit nearly any dynamics.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.25
data existence: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.48
data adequacy: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim imports the free-energy principle from nervous systems to cells in development and treats it as true of both. Expression and behavioral time series exist, and they underdetermine the objective a system is optimizing. A successful active-inference fit does not rule out simpler homeostasis. No measurement distinguishes the claim from a non-cognitive account of the same developmental path.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Developmental trajectories and neural activity can be fit by a variational free-energy objective. Other control laws fit the same series once latent states are free, so no public time series isolates surprise minimization.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Embryonic cells do not come with an observed generative model.

Free-energy minimization is flexible enough to accommodate many trajectories.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.15
discriminating power: 0.1
data adequacy: 0.05
operationalizability: 0.3
data existence: 0.05
